text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic initiated adoption of a special law to recognise part of local election results according to te OSCE report.
- President Milosevic received trade union representatives and said everyone should work the best they can and as much as they can.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic said Milosevic's decision provides condition for peace to return to the streets.
- Local authorities in Serb-controlled region of Eastern Slavonia and Western Srem in Croatia suspended work after unfavourable U.N. Security Council report.

- Serbs living in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia are leaving the region because of fear and insecurity, said Doug Koffman, spokesman for U.N. Transitional Administration in region. Last weekend 47 Serb families left the region.
- Yugoslavia needs $29 billion by the year 2020 for development of its energy system.

- Insolvency of Yugoslav economy could be solved by opening branch of prominent European bank where citizens and firms could with confidence deposit their money, said Miloje Kanjevac, head of private consulting firm FINIS.
- Jovan Zebic, federal deputy prime minister, announced further liberalisation of imports but also protection measures for domestic industries.
- Serbia's educational workers resume strike. More than 1,000 schools still closed.
NASA BORBA
- Slobodan Vucetic, constitutional court judge, said President Milosevic's initiative with regard to recognition of local election results is not in keeping with the constitution.
- U.S. State Department sceptical on Milosevic's readiness to reinstate opposition victory in local elections.
- Serbian authorities' measures exclude Serbia from Europe, delegation of Europaan Forum said after visiting Belgrade.
- Belgrade bar association demands police removed from streets.

- Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic will call for extraordinary parliament session beginning of next week to discuss reconstruction and reduction of republican government, source close to government said.
BLIC
- Belgrade bakeries say bread price must rise due to current wheat shortage.
